newsitem.title: USA: US, EU halt talks on mutual recognition agreements.
newsitem.headline: US, EU halt talks on mutual recognition agreements.

text.p: The United States and the European Union have suspended talks on agreements to allow each other's agencies test, inspect and certify certain products like pharmaceuticals, a U.S. official said on Sunday.

"We suspended negotiations yesterday afternoon after we were unable to reach agreement and there are still outstanding issues in the ares of pharmaceuticals and medical equipment," said the official, who asked not to be identified.

The talks covered so-called mutual recognition agreements that would allow agencies in the United States to perform procedures like testing, inspection and certification to EU requirements, and vice versa.
The areas covered by the talks, whose latest round was in Washington, include pharmaceuticals, medical devices, telecommunications, information technology and sports craft.
A U.S. official said last week the two sides hoped to have an agreement in place by this Wednesday's U.S.-EU summit in the Netherlands, which President Bill Clinton will attend.

The official contacted on Sunday declined to predict the chances of a deal being in place by then, adding the issue may be discussed by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan on the margins of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development's annual ministerial meeting on Monday and Tuesday in Paris.

One official close to the talks said that from the U.S. point of view the main sticking points were EU demands on the testing and certification of pharmaceuticals products and medical equipment which the United States believed would lower U.S. consumer standards.
